key_facts: Permit required before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes covered by a wall or buried in the ground (exemptions in SF Plumbing Code §104.2).
Allowed contractor classes: C4, C16, C20, C36, C54, B (after approval based on scope), or A.
Homeowner self-application restricted to property owners of stand-alone single-family dwellings (R-3 occupancy).
Permit Center help desk: 628-652-4900 and permitsf@sfgov.org.
Lists 'Minor repairs to existing interior plaster or wallboard, unless they are required for fire protection' among work not needing a building permit.
Lists 'Painting, papering and similar finish work' among work not needing a building permit.

Applies to home improvement contracts where aggregate contract price for labor, services, and materials exceeds $500 (§7159(b)), unless governed by a conforming §7159.10 service and repair contract (§7159(a)(2)).
Prime or direct contractor is administratively responsible for completion of the project in accordance with the contract, plans, and specifications (§7159(a)(5)(B)).
Governs buyer-initiated service and repair contracts of $750 or less where no payment is due or accepted until the work is completed (§7159.10(a)(1)(A)–(D)).
Requires signed, dated written contract before any work starts, stating contractor name, address, license number, and Commercial General Liability (CGL) insurance notice (§7159.10(d)(4)–(7)).
Permits landlord entry during normal business hours to make necessary or agreed repairs (§1954(a)(2), (b)).

Requires written notice (24 hours presumed reasonable; 6 days if mailed) stating date, approximate time, and purpose, or oral agreement with tenant for agreed repairs within one week (§1954(d)(1), (3)).

Defines C-9 Drywall Contractor as laying out and installing gypsum wallboard and assemblies, nonstructural metal framing, and taping and texturing operations to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.
